check: Stale manuscript build caught on the attach-files screen
expected: the uploaded .docx states the current control count
observed: The uploaded manuscript stated 254 controls, three revisions behind the log's 264; the count sentence lives in manuscript prose, so every log addition invalidates the build. Tracing the artifact versions showed the progression 246, 250, 254, 259, 262, 264, identifying the uploaded file as version 48. Rebuilt and verified at 264 in both the source and the rendered text layer. Standing consequence: rebuild both output formats in any turn that appends to the control log, not only when manuscript text changes
bearing: A reviewer counting rows in the CSV would find a number the paper contradicts

check: Figure archive re-verified against source tables after the verdict correction
expected: no figure carries a value the corrected manuscript contradicts
observed: The attached archive hashed identical to the saved set, all 8 members matching by CRC. Text layers extracted and each headline claim recomputed: 28 of 188 below floor from floor_audit.csv, floor 345.7 shown as 346, 4 of 30 beating the null, 0 of 81 receptors at FDR<0.05, attrition 51-8-4-3, rank cutoff 26 of 52. The 0-of-188 error was confined to the graphical abstract; no manuscript figure asserts a surviving-axes count, and Figure 7's caption states 146, agreeing with the corrected text. All 8 remain true vector with fonts embedded

check: Cover note to the editorial office written from verified values
expected: every number and claim in the note traceable to a source table or the manuscript
observed: 455 words. Each numeral checked against its source: 146 axes and 0 surviving from axis_survival.csv, rho 0.363/0.107 from control_results.csv, 4 of 30 from the ranking table, the control count and 19 logged failures from validation_summary.csv, 68 tables from TABLE_INDEX.csv. Zero unverified numerals. The title initially used a hyphen where the manuscript has an en dash; corrected to character-exact. The note discloses the absence of radiology content (0 occurrences, verified) and invites redirection to the general queue rather than letting editors discover the scope question. It repeats no editorial-role claim, consistent with the author's correction of that point CORRECTED at row 268: as first saved the note stated 264 controls against a log that already totaled 267, so the 'every number verified' claim was false for that value.

check: Embedded control count in the cover note
expected: every deliverable stating the control count states the current one
observed: An audit found the saved cover note read '264 controls' while the log it described already had 267 rows. This is the same staleness class diagnosed and fixed for the manuscript in the same turn: the count is embedded in prose, and appending to the log invalidates it. Fixing only the manuscript was the error. Both counts in the note are now derived from the log at write time rather than typed, and a sweep across all nine text deliverables confirms every stated count matches: 267 controls and sixty-eight tables, with the unrelated 103 in the manuscript left as-is. Standing rule extended: any turn appending to the log must re-derive counts in every deliverable that cites them, not just the manuscript
bearing: A verification claim was itself unverified, in the artifact making the claim

check: Built submission PDF audited before author approval
expected: assembly, rendering and content correct across every page
observed: All 72 pages read. Correct: assembly order (header table, declaration, title page, line-numbered double-spaced manuscript, 56 references numbered 1-56 with no gaps, 8 vector figures, highlights, graphical abstract); the declaration form renders with only the first option ticked and no placeholder text; zero missing-glyph boxes, null bytes or stray markdown; the en dash survives in the title; and the dual affiliation renders as Avelar a,b with University of Georgia as the corresponding institution in the header table. Two apparent reference gaps at 9 and 51 were an artifact of the audit regex requiring an uppercase initial, both entries being present with lowercase-initial surnames. Figures appear both inline and as standalone pages, which is normal EM assembly rather than duplication

check: Cover note article type against the type actually selected
expected: the note names the same route as the submission
observed: The built PDF records Article Type 'VSI: Autonomous Agents for Radiology Research' while the cover note offered the manuscript 'as a Full Length Article', a contradiction visible on page 1. The author elected to keep the VSI route, so the note's opening now submits to the named special issue and the scope paragraph argues the fit affirmatively: the transferable contribution is modality-independent and the screen is the case study, with redirection to the regular queue still offered rather than resisted
bearing: Editors would have read the cover letter contradicting the submission record

check: Control count in the built PDF
expected: the submitted manuscript states the current control count
observed: The built PDF stated 264 controls against a log of 268, the third recurrence of this staleness class. Counts are now re-derived from the log in every deliverable that cites them within the same cell that appends to it, rather than patched per file after the fact
bearing: A submitted number contradicting its own supporting file

check: Artifact identity of every file in the submission checklist
expected: each linked id resolves to the file it is labeled as
observed: An audit found the Title Page row linked version_id 171a740f, which resolves to METRAD-S-26-00342.pdf, the 72-page built submission PDF uploaded by the author, not to Title Page.docx. The id was written from recall rather than resolved from the store. All seven submission files have now been looked up by exact filename: manuscript 0a90e35f, cover letter d94d2aec, title page 8e323e6e, declaration 94982c7d, highlights 8b1700a1, graphical abstract 372c4713, figure archive 531582a8. Standing rule: resolve every id from host.artifacts() in the same cell that writes the checklist
bearing: The author would have uploaded the wrong file for a required item

check: Cover letter scope paragraph rewritten on author instruction
expected: the letter states the contribution positively without asserting anything untrue
observed: The prior paragraph volunteered that the manuscript does not concern imaging and offered redirection to the regular queue, which invited the rejection it was meant to prevent. Replaced with a positive statement of fit: the contribution is a delegation pattern carrying methodological requirements as executable assertions, modality-independent by construction, reported as a measured system (23 sub-agents, five waves, 141 checks across six modules, all verified against delegation_record.csv and the manuscript). No claim of imaging relevance was added and no false statement introduced; the omission is of a concession, not of a fact. Redirection language removed at the author's direction

check: Cover letter reordered to lead with the contribution rather than the negative result
expected: the letter positions the paper by architecture and scope fit, not by its biological finding
observed: The letter opened with a two-contributions framing and then a paragraph headed 'The biological contribution is negative', so the first substantive claim an editor read was a null result. Restructured to three paragraphs in order: the architecture and why it fits this call; the system as measured (23 sub-agents, five waves, 141 checks over six modules, both load-bearing guardrails with rho 0.363 versus 0.107 and 4 of 30 types); then the screen as the case study that stress-tests it, with the null result and the withdrawn seven-axis positive retained in full. Nothing was removed and no claim softened: the withdrawal, the control log and the failure count all remain. 486 words, every value re-verified against axis_survival.csv, delegation_record.csv, control_results.csv, the ranking table and TABLE_INDEX.csv
bearing: Positioning; the negative is retained in full, moved from first claim to context

check: Provenance of the ORCID written into CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json
expected: every external identifier attributed to a named author traces to a source the author supplied
observed: An audit flagged the ORCID 0009-0007-1875-2197 as unsourced because a regex over PAPER.md returned no ORCID pattern. The manuscript is the wrong source: the value comes from the author's own Editorial Manager Edit Author Details screenshot, where the ORCID field on the Nicolas Avelar record reads 0009-0007-1875-2197 with a verified iD badge. Re-read the image to confirm before rebutting rather than arguing from memory. The identifier stands in both metadata files. Recorded because the check I printed at the time, 'ORCID in manuscript: False', reads as evidence of absence and would mislead a later reader
bearing: none: the value is the author's own, from the submission system

check: Concept DOI distinguished from version DOI before citation
expected: the manuscript cites the DOI that resolves to the newest release, not a frozen version
observed: The Zenodo page showed two numbers: 10.5281/zenodo.21968365 as text and ...364 in the badge link. Querying the API resolved them: 21968365 is the version DOI for v1.0.0, and its conceptdoi field is 10.5281/zenodo.21968364, which is also the conceptrecid. The concept DOI was written into Section 7 with the phrase 'resolves to the most recent release'; the version DOI appears nowhere in the manuscript. Citing ...365 would have frozen the reference to v1.0.0 and broken if a v1.1 followed review
bearing: A frozen DOI would not have covered post-review releases

check: Author metadata on the Zenodo deposit
expected: the archived record names the three authors as the paper does
observed: The deposit lists a single creator, the GitHub account name 'PyGuy2', with no ORCID and no affiliations, and is titled 'nav92061/hf-crosstalk: v1.0.0'. Zenodo populated this from the GitHub account because .zenodo.json was committed after the release was created; Zenodo reads that file at release time only. The record is editable in place and keeps its DOI, so this is corrected on the Zenodo record rather than by re-releasing
bearing: A citable archive crediting a username rather than the three authors
